targets.name: Barnard's Star
targets.kind: Nearby red dwarf — the fastest proper motion of any star (≈10.4″/yr)
targets.tip: Very bright: its core saturates SPHEREx. Turn on motion tracking or compare the first and last epochs to see it march north.

targets.name: Epsilon Indi B
targets.kind: Pair of brown dwarfs (Ba/Bb) orbiting the star ε Indi A
targets.tip: Cold brown dwarfs are brightest at long wavelengths: try detectors D5–D6 or the colour mode. Open a 15′ field to include the host star ε Indi A.

targets.name: WISE 0855−0714
targets.kind: Coldest known brown dwarf, fast-moving (challenge position 08h55m10.831s −7°14′42.53″)
targets.tip: Very faint below 3 µm. Use D5–D6, co-add each survey and difference the epochs.
targets.posNote: Centre from the WiseView link in the challenge resources

targets.name: RW Aurigae
targets.kind: Young variable binary star (T Tauri type)
targets.tip: Open the light curve: brightness changes between epochs show up at the same wavelength.

targets.name: R Draconis
targets.tip: Large-amplitude variable. Compare spectra from different surveys.
